title: 8. Technicals, Stage 2 Posture & Options Overlay

epigraph.quote: Never confuse an oversold dead-cat bounce inside a broken Stage 4 downtrend with a durable Stage 1 base; until price reclaims rising moving averages on institutional accumulation, capital preservation comes first.
epigraph.author: Quantitative Tape & Stage 2 Desk

web_blocks.html: NVIDIA's technical structure requires explicit reconciliation across two verified dates: the November 20, 2026 session close (facts_US_2026-11-20.json) and the November 23, 2026 live TradingView snapshot (snapshots_US_2026-11-20.json). On November 20, NVDA plunged -14.01% to $125.53 on 626.37M shares (2.41x 20D average volume. 630.31M / 2.80x 30D avg), sitting -39.4% (-39.36%) below its 50-day SMA ($207.00) and -38.27% below its 200-day SMA ($203.35) with 1D RSI14 at 15.05, 1W RSI at 25.01, and 4H RSI at 14.95. By November 23, NVDA staged a sharp +32.5% reflex bounce to $166.33 on 529.24M shares (2.20x 30D avg), yet stage2_evaluation classifies the stock as STAGE_4 (AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN / CAP_REJECTED) because price remains -19.30% below its falling 50-day SMA ($206.11), -19.63% below its 30-week SMA ($206.95), and -9.82% below its 10-week EMA ($184.44).

The broader U.S. Market regime reinforces this caution. As of November 20, 2026, the S&P 500 is in a confirmed Downtrend with only 38.8% breadth above the 50-day moving average (46.9% above the 200-day moving average), 10 distribution days in the trailing 25 sessions, and a 5.04% 10-year Treasury yield (+28 bps 2s/10s spread). In a Downtrend regime with 9 stock-level distribution days in 25 sessions, sharp single-day bounces like November 23's move to $166.33 frequently resolve as Stage 4 bear-market rallies rather than V-shaped bottoms.

web_blocks.title: Stage 4 & Options Discipline: Zero Capital Deployment
paragraphs: CAP_REJECTED prohibits IMMEDIATE_BUY and ACCUMULATE_ON_DIP, and our unbiased re-underwriting upgrades the technical rejection to REJECTED (TIER_0) rather than hedging with WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT.

Options are likewise DECLINED (NO_OPTIONS_EDGE, 1.03:1 R:R on $165/$175 spread). No equity or options order should be staged until NVDA builds a multi-week Stage 1 base above rising 10-week and 30-week averages and clears its FY27 Form 10-K audit.

book_paragraphs: Technical analysis does not predict corporate earnings, but it measures institutional conviction with ruthless precision. Between November 20 and November 23, 2026, NVIDIA's tape illustrated the classic anatomy of a Stage 4 liquidation followed by a violent reflex bounce. On November 20, the stock closed at $125.53—down 14.01 percent on the day and 39.36 percent below its 50-day simple moving average ($207.00)—testing its 52-week low of $124.50 on 626.37 million shares. Because the quantitative facts ledger tags proximity to 52-week lows as Stage 1 (Basing), the November 20 screen recorded Stage 1. By November 23, shares surged 32.5 percent to $166.33 on 529.24 million shares, yet the live Stage 2 evaluation engine classifies NVIDIA as STAGE_4 (AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN / CAP_REJECTED).

Why does STAGE_4 govern our capital decision even after a 32.5 percent single-day bounce? Because $166.33 still sits 19.30 percent below a falling 50-day SMA ($206.11), 19.63 percent below the 30-week SMA ($206.95), and 9.82 percent below the 10-week EMA ($184.44). Furthermore, the S&P 500 itself sits in a confirmed Downtrend with 38.8 percent breadth above the 50-day moving average and 10 distribution days in 25 sessions. Stage 4 bear-market rallies routinely retrace 20 to 35 percent before rolling over into secondary lows when overhead supply at the 50-day and 200-day moving averages is tested.

book_subsections.title: Why Stage 4 Bear-Market Rallies Trap Bottom-Fishers
paragraphs: One of the most costly errors in institutional equity management is mistaking a sharp oversold rebound inside a Stage 4 decline for the start of a new Stage 2 advance. When a mega-cap leader falls 48.42 percent from $243.37 to $124.50 in six weeks, short-covering and tactical mean-reversion desks inevitably trigger violent counter-trend rallies. NVIDIA's 32.5 percent surge from $125.53 on November 20 to $166.33 on November 23 demonstrates how quickly extreme oversold oscillators—1D RSI14 at 15.05 and 4H RSI at 14.95—can snap back toward neutral.

Yet price action alone does not repair broken institutional trend structure. Even at $166.33, NVIDIA trades 19.30 percent below its falling 50-day simple moving average ($206.11) and 19.63 percent below its 30-week simple moving average ($206.95). Every institutional portfolio manager who bought shares between $180 and $243 during the autumn now sits underwater, creating layers of overhead supply whenever the stock approaches the $181.67 to $209.20 zone. In a healthy Stage 1 base, volatility contracts, daily trading ranges narrow well below 3 percent, and moving averages flatten out over several months as weak hands finish selling. By contrast, NVIDIA's 14-day ATR sits at $13.22—nearly 8 percent of share price—while the S&P 500 itself remains in a confirmed Downtrend with 10 distribution days in 25 sessions.

For these reasons, our technical framework enforces CAP_REJECTED and refuses to deploy either equity or option premium into the bounce. In options, the updated live chain confirms NO_OPTIONS_EDGE: a $165/$175 call spread costs $4.93 for only $5.07 maximum profit (1.03:1 reward-to-risk), failing our 1.25:1 minimum threshold. Retiring all prior conditional $124.50 triggers protects the portfolio from paying high implied volatility for a directional bet against a falling 50-day moving average.

book_subsections.title: Stage 1 Base-Building Checklist Before Re-Entry
paragraphs: For NVIDIA to earn a future technical upgrade from REJECTED, four observable conditions must align on weekly and daily charts. First, daily volatility must compress as the stock carves a multi-week horizontal base without breaking the $124.50 capitulation low. Second, the 50-day simple moving average ($206.11) and 30-week simple moving average ($206.95) must stop declining and flatten out. Third, price must reclaim the 10-week EMA ($184.44) and 30-week SMA on above-average accumulation volume rather than short-covering spikes. Fourth, the S&P 500 breadth regime must improve from Downtrend (38.8% above 50DMA) back into a confirmed uptrend. Until those four gates clear simultaneously, capital preservation remains paramount.

book_subsections.title: Dual-Date Tape Anatomy: Capitulation Low vs. Reflex Rebound
paragraphs: Comparing the November 20 and November 23 tape snapshots highlights why quantitative stage rules require discipline. On November 20, 2026, NVIDIA closed at $125.53—down 14.01 percent in a single session on 626.37 million shares—after testing an intraday 52-week low of $124.50. At that close, shares sat 39.36 percent below the 50-day SMA ($207.00), 38.27 percent below the 200-day SMA ($203.35), and 39.65 percent below the 30-week SMA ($208.02). Because the quantitative facts screen classifies stocks sitting at 52-week lows as Stage 1 (Basing), the facts ledger tagged NVDA as Stage 1.

Three days later, on November 23, 2026, NVIDIA surged 32.5 percent to $166.33 on 529.24 million shares, lifting 1D RSI from 15.05 to 43.47 and 1W RSI from 25.01 to 41.05. Despite that dramatic bounce, the live Stage 2 evaluation engine classifies NVDA as STAGE_4 (AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN / CAP_REJECTED). Why? Because price remains 19.30 percent below the falling 50-day SMA ($206.11), 19.63 percent below the 30-week SMA ($206.95), and 9.82 percent below the 10-week EMA ($184.44). Meanwhile, the screen's Stage 2 support buy zone sits at $181.67 to $209.20 with a $199.50 invalidation stop—meaning the stock is still trapped well below institutional support. Until price reclaims those moving averages on sustained accumulation, both equity and options remain off-limits.

In addition, our options overlay confirms that implied volatility remains elevated relative to realistic upside reward. Paying $4.93 for a $165/$175 call spread yields at most $5.07 in net profit (1.03:1 reward-to-risk), failing our 1.25:1 minimum threshold. Standing aside preserves 100 percent of option capital.

Institutional tape history also underscores why single-day rallies after steep drops require skepticism. During major technology drawdowns in 2000–2002 and 2022, leading semiconductor and software stocks repeatedly staged 20 to 35 percent one-week bounces off oversold daily RSI readings below 20, only to roll over once they reached falling 50-day moving averages. On November 23, NVIDIA closed at $166.33—still $39.78 below its falling 50-day SMA ($206.11) and $40.62 below its 30-week SMA ($206.95). Until weekly closing prices establish higher lows above the $124.50 shelf and reclaim the 10-week EMA ($184.44) on rising volume, the primary trend remains down.
